The most frequent error is treating "safe" as "automatic." Because Over 1.5 clears in most matches, it's tempting to back it on every fixture on the card without regard for the specific matchup. That approach erodes an edge rather than building one — the market only holds up statistically when selections are filtered, not blanket-applied. A second common mistake is ignoring team news entirely. A side missing its two most productive attackers, or fielding a heavily rotated line-up for a fixture [...] ### 

Analysts review recent attacking form, head-to-head goal trends, and defensive record for both sides, and avoid fixtures between two historically low-scoring or defensively disciplined teams, even at short odds.

### 

Yes, and it's a common way to use this market, but stacking many legs still compounds risk even when each individual leg looks safe. Size the accumulator to your bankroll rather than chasing the highest possible combined odds.

### [...] Volume is easy to produce. Discipline is not. A reliable Over 1.5 service publishes selections with enough lead time to compare odds across bookmakers, reviews team news before kickoff rather than relying on data pulled the night before, and is transparent when a run of results goes badly rather than quietly removing the evidence.
